feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital/platform leadership in mission-driven organizations. It communicates scope and progression well, but it is somewhat dense and repetitive, with a few style inconsistencies and limited outcome-focused evidence beyond activity descriptions.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear leadership narrative: strong progression within NACo into senior digital ownership across web, analytics, governance, multimedia, and AI-enabled search.  
- Good credibility signals: specific platforms, tools, scale metrics (10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers), and concrete project examples.  
- Writing is generally polished and professional, with a consistent strategic tone aligned to public-sector communications roles.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily. Consolidating these would improve structure and readability.  
- Add more impact/results language: several bullets describe responsibilities rather than outcomes. Include measurable improvements in engagement, efficiency, adoption, cost savings, or campaign performance.  
- Fix stylistic consistency issues: use one spelling standard for “organization-wide/organisation-wide” (currently consistent to US, keep that throughout); standardize list punctuation around “web, email, social, and multimedia” vs no serial comma elsewhere; “10×20-foot” may read oddly—consider “10 x 20-foot.” No major misspellings or grammar errors found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and domain focus, but it’s slightly dense and repeats themes already covered in the subtitle, competencies, and work experience. Tightening it and adding one concrete scale cue would improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Consider: “Digital platform and communications leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing high-volume public-sector websites, governance models, and content operations. Leads enterprise web transformation, analytics and reporting infrastructure, editorial workflows, multimedia production, and AI-enabled search and content experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.”
- Replace “building the platforms” with more direct outcome-oriented language like “modernizing” or “leading transformation of.”
- Change “AI-enabled user experiences” to “AI-enabled search and content experiences” to align more closely with the recent project and technical skills.
- If space allows, add a scale signal such as “10,000+ page websites” or “3.5M annual page views.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital leader” overlaps with the subtitle; consider using the intro to emphasize scope/results instead.
- “Governance models,” “analytics infrastructure,” and “multimedia production” are repeated in Core Competencies/Topline Skills.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header and Topline Skills. It would be sharper if it emphasized distinctive capability areas and used tighter, more parallel phrasing.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use more concise, category-style wording with consistent structure: Enterprise web modernization • Governance and editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Workflow automation and platform integration • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Multi-channel communications operations • Public-sector and advocacy communications • Multimedia and livestream production
- Replace “content experiences” with “content discovery” to sound more specific and credible alongside search.
- Consider “Public-sector and advocacy communications” over “Advocacy and public-sector communications” for smoother phrasing.
- Keep the list focused on strategic strengths; avoid mixing broad leadership areas with tool-level execution.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise website modernization,” “AI-enabled search,” “analytics infrastructure,” and “multimedia production” are already strongly covered in the header and Topline Skills.
- “Digital governance & editorial systems” closely repeats “Editorial systems and governance” in Topline Skills.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshots, but the block is text-dense and overlaps with the NACo experience section. Tightening phrasing and foregrounding outcomes or scope will make it feel more additive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add dates or “Selected recent projects” framing to reinforce recency and distinguish this from core experience.
- Use parallel, tighter phrasing: “Built,” “Led,” “Developed,” “Launched,” and trim stacked descriptors.
- Add 1 concrete outcome, audience, or scale detail where possible (for example, users, campaign reach, conference/event context, or organizational purpose).
- Rewrite for consistency: “10'×20'” or “10 x 20-foot,” and consider “AI-powered” instead of repeating “AI-enabled.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite development, and advocacy video series closely repeat achievements already covered in NACo roles.
- The anniversary campaign adds the most fresh detail; consider keeping only the most distinct 2–3 projects in the footer.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: coleman@colemanpdavis.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant recent role, but it reads broad and overlaps heavily with your prior NACo leadership entry. Tighten it around what is new in the consulting scope—especially AI search, Drupal campaign builds, and enterprise workflow improvements.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper scope statement: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, Drupal platform enhancements, content operations, and cross-channel governance as an external consultant.”
- Replace generic verbs (“consult,” “advise,” “deliver”) with outcome-oriented phrasing: “Designed,” “implemented,” “streamlined,” “launched,” “led.”
- Break out 3–4 high-value bullets, e.g.:
- Led an AI-enabled search initiative, defining retrieval strategy, structured content requirements, and discovery UX for member-facing content.
- Built Drupal-based campaign and storytelling experiences, including reusable microsite templates, modular content components, and downloadable toolkits.
- Improved digital workflows, analytics, and governance to support coordinated communications across web, email, social, and multimedia.
- Add metrics if available: number of sites/pages/templates, time saved, adoption by teams, search performance, or engagement gains.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Governance, workflows, analytics” repeats the Director of Digital Media entry; keep this version focused on consultant-specific initiatives.
- “CMS development/front-end implementation” may duplicate skills sections unless tied to a concrete project or result.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize enterprise ownership and outcomes while avoiding overlap with the adjacent NACo roles on newsletters, video, and general digital operations.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper scope statement: “Directed NACo’s enterprise digital communications function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Combine and prioritize the strongest achievements: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make outcomes more explicit where possible: add % improvements in publishing efficiency, reporting speed, engagement, production cost savings, or reduced vendor reliance from the in-house studio.
- Tighten softer bullets: change “Strengthened digital operations…” to a result-led line such as “Implemented governance, publishing standards, and cross-department planning systems to improve consistency and coordination.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry at the enterprise/leadership level.
- Video studio language may duplicate older video-production bullets unless framed as a new capability built at director level.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry reads broad and overlaps with the more senior NACo roles. Tighten it around executional leadership, channel ownership, and systems/process improvements, with any concrete audience or output metrics you can add.

Suggested edit
- Open with scope + function: “Managed day-to-day digital communications across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, supporting advocacy messaging and organization-wide editorial execution.”
- Replace “helping” phrasing with direct action: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Combine video/editorial workflow points into sharper impact bullets: “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.” / “Improved editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams.”
- If possible, add measurable outcomes: newsletter open/click rates, video cadence/views, turnaround time, or number of teams/stakeholders coordinated.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid repeating high-level channel oversight already covered in Director of Digital Media.
- “Weekly video updates” also appears in the 2015–2018 role; distinguish this entry as scaling/formalizing the program.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this skills block is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header, core competencies, and recent NACo roles. It should sharpen the highest-value positioning and use more distinctive, outcome-oriented phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad labels with tighter, differentiated terms: “Enterprise digital strategy,” “Editorial governance and publishing operations,” “Cross-channel communications leadership,” “Public-sector and advocacy storytelling,” “Audience and content strategy.”
- Consider a more modern rewrite: “Enterprise digital strategy • Editorial governance and content operations • Cross-channel communications leadership • Public-sector and advocacy storytelling • Audience-centered content strategy”
- Use “content operations” instead of “content planning” to better reflect seniority and match recent experience building workflows, governance, and systems.
- If space allows, prioritize terms tied to recent impact: “Drupal modernization,” “analytics-informed strategy,” or “AI-enabled content discovery” rather than older/general messaging language.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “governance,” and “multi-channel communications” already appear in the header and Core Competencies.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with Core Competencies’ “Advocacy and public-sector communications.”

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it reads as a generic tool list and overlaps heavily with the Technical + IT section. For a topline skills area, emphasize higher-value capabilities and recent strengths rather than listing every platform.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability-led phrasing, e.g. “Drupal and CMS modernization” instead of separate platform names.
- Cut lower-priority or older items here if they already appear in Technical + IT; keep only the most relevant to recent work.
- Group related items for clarity: “Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint and Power Pages • CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- If possible, align to proven outcomes from recent roles, e.g. “Drupal modernization for 10,000+ page sites” or “AI-enabled search and structured content workflows.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Technical + IT”; avoid repeating the same platform list in both places.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” already appears in the header and Core Competencies, so keep wording distinct or shorten here.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it reads as a duplicate of the “Technical + IT” analytics section and misses the leadership/decision-support angle that better fits a topline skills block. Make it more outcome-oriented and slightly more strategic.

Suggested edit
- Reframe from tool inventory to capability statement: “Analytics strategy, dashboarding and performance optimization.”
- Tighten and group items: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity.”
- Replace generic phrases with executive-value language: “KPI framework development,” “executive/leadership reporting,” “insight generation for content and platform decisions.”
- Suggested rewrite: “Analytics strategy and reporting • GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity • KPI framework development • Executive dashboards and leadership reporting • SEO, UX and content performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This largely duplicates “Technical + IT > Data, Analytics & Optimization”; keep this version strategic and let the Technical section hold the fuller tool list.
- “Dashboarding” appears in Technical + IT, so avoid repeating that exact term unless you remove it there.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads generic and overlaps with the Core Competencies line and several NACo role bullets. Make it more senior, specific, and oriented to delivery capability rather than listing basic tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to emphasize leadership-level execution: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ camera and studio systems • Virtual event operations”
- Replace “Video production and editing” with a more distinctive phrase like “Broadcast-quality video production” or “End-to-end video production” to signal scale/quality.
- Consider tightening to 4 items max and grouping related terms: “Livestream, hybrid and virtual event production” instead of splitting them.
- If you can support it elsewhere, add scale-oriented language such as “in-house studio production” or “recurring advocacy programming.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies; avoid repeating the exact phrase.
- “Studio operations” and video production are already evidenced in the Director of Digital Media entry, so this skills line should stay concise rather than restating accomplishments.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Since recent experience is strongly Drupal-led, the ordering should reflect that and avoid repeating the same skills section verbatim.

Suggested edit
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages** is fine if Drupal remains first; consider adding light context: **Drupal (enterprise/public-sector), WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages**.
- If space allows, make it outcome-oriented rather than a bare list: **CMS platforms: Drupal (10,000+ page migration; microsites), WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages**.
- Keep naming consistent with the rest of the CV: use either **CMS** or **Platforms** terminology consistently across sections.
- Consider dropping **GitHub Pages** if it’s not materially used in recent roles; it currently feels less central than the others.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This item substantially duplicates **Topline Skills → Web Platforms & Technical Execution**.
- Avoid repeating Drupal/WordPress/SharePoint in multiple skills sections unless one version adds context or scale.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” For a senior, recent-profile CV, this item should emphasize implementation scope and modern tools rather than basic coding terms alone.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe as a tighter, more senior-oriented list: “Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API and tag management integrations • Edge/serverless scripting (Cloudflare Workers) • Deployment automation (GitHub Actions)”
- Drop version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless required; they add little value at this level.
- If accurate, add one qualifier tied to recent work, e.g. “for Drupal-based public-sector sites” or “for campaign microsites and analytics workflows.”
- Consider replacing “Google Tag Manager” with “Tag management (Google Tag Manager)” to group it as a capability, not just a tool.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- “Workflow automation” appears elsewhere; avoid adding similar phrasing here unless this section becomes more implementation-specific.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems leadership. Tighten it to emphasize automation platforms over general collaboration tools and align with the stronger “workflow automation” story in recent roles.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to group by function: “Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira/Asana/Trello • Slack/Teams”
- Consider renaming to: “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Systems” or “Automation, PM & Collaboration Tools”
- Prioritize higher-signal tools first: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana; move Basecamp/Trello later or remove if less current
- If space allows, add light context instead of a pure list: “Built workflow and reporting systems in Airtable, Power Automate and Zapier; managed cross-team operations in Jira, Asana, Slack and Teams”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing verbatim
- Slack, Teams, and Basecamp are lower-impact unless tied to process ownership; they can dilute the stronger automation narrative

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too bare to add much value on its own. It should signal level of use and enterprise relevance, especially since email leadership already appears in recent NACo roles.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize platform administration/operations rather than just listing tools: “Email & Engagement Platforms: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp”
- If accurate, add scope qualifiers: “enterprise email operations,” “newsletter distribution,” “journey/campaign setup,” or “member communications platforms.”
- Put the strongest/most current platform first; if Dynamics 365 is most recent and strategic, keep it first.
- Consider a more impact-oriented version if your format allows: “Managed email and member-engagement platforms including Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys, Higher Logic and Mailchimp for newsletter, campaign and audience communications.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This overlaps with work-experience bullets about leading email newsletters and digital channels; avoid repeating audience-size claims here.
- “Multi-channel communications operations” already appears in Core Competencies, so keep this item tool-specific.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is too generic and duplicates the “Analytics, Insights & Optimization” topline skills almost exactly. Use this section for sharper technical specificity, not broad capability labels.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **GA4 • Google Tag Manager • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Microsoft Clarity • SEO analysis • Experimentation**
- Replace vague nouns like **A/B testing** and **Dashboarding** with stronger, more technical phrasing such as **Experimentation** or **Reporting dashboards**.
- If space allows elsewhere, move outcomes to recent roles instead of this skills line, e.g., analytics stack supporting **3.5M annual page views** and leadership reporting.
- Consider ordering by depth/relevance: **GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Microsoft Clarity, Google Tag Manager, SEO analysis, Experimentation**.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially repeats **Topline Skills [3] Analytics, Insights & Optimization**.
- **SEO** may also overlap with broader strategy language in competencies; keep it here only if you’ve used it directly.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and reads as setup rather than impact. Tighten it around team-building, platform work, and recurring multimedia output, with any available scale metrics.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground advancement and outcomes: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and improve workflows across web, email, social and video.”
- Split the rest into 1–2 concrete achievements: website refresh contribution; launched/produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates.
- Add measurable scope where possible: number of livestreams/videos, audience reach, website traffic, email list size, or team size supervised.
- Use stronger verbs and cut filler like “high-impact” and “day-to-day guidance.”

Possible rewrite:
- Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital team and streamline publishing workflows across web, email, social and video.
- Supported a major website refresh and produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates that expanded NACo’s in-house multimedia capacity.
- Provided informal supervision and workflow support to a digital media associate.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating “weekly advocacy video update” language from the 2018–2022 role unless this entry clarifies it began here.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a credible “first podcast” achievement, but it reads generic and overlaps with later multimedia/digital roles. Tighten it to emphasize coordination, innovation support, and the podcast as the clearest distinct outcome.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the standout result: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities; launched the organization’s first podcast, leading planning, scripting, and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” with a more active, specific verb: “produced” or “supported development of digital and multimedia content.”
- If possible, add scope or output: number of projects supported, podcast episodes launched, audiences reached, or teams/stakeholders coordinated.
- Keep this entry shorter than later NACo roles so the progression into digital leadership remains clear.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later video/multimedia bullets; keep this item focused on research/innovation coordination plus the first podcast.
- Avoid overemphasizing digital leadership here, since stronger evidence appears in 2015–2024 roles.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but currently mixes software with capabilities, and it overlaps heavily with “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery” in Topline Skills. Tightening it to tool names plus one or two specific production environments will make it cleaner and less repetitive.
